FAST
Nov 1 : MotoGP officials told teams on Sunday they had received no information warranting a change to next weekend's Qatar Grand Prix despite pushback from riders concerned about going there during the war against Iran, but Yamaha have withdrawn.
The race at the Lusail International Circuit, originally scheduled for April, was postponed to November 6 to 8 due to the conflict, which has spread through much of the region, beyond the initial US-Israeli attacks on Iran.
A group of riders had sought more assurances over travel to the Gulf region, such as details on evacuation plans and indemnity insurance.
"This morning MotoGP management met with the teams to review the latest information and assurances provided by the State of Qatar, Lusail International Circuit, relevant embassies and independent experts," a MotoGP spokesperson told Reuters.

"These internal and external assessments continue to inform our ongoing risk review and decision-making process.
"Following a review of the latest information, official assurances from the State of Qatar and independent assessments available to us at this moment, we have received no information that would warrant a change to the current plans for the event."
The International Road Racing Teams Association, which represents all MotoGP teams and helps in coordinating paddock logistics, also attended the meeting.
YAMAHA WITHDRAWS FROM QATAR GP
Yamaha, who had been awaiting instructions following a Japanese government advisory that urged citizens to refrain from non-essential travel to the Gulf nation, will not go to Qatar, citing "company-wide travel restrictions".
"MotoGP is disappointed by Yamaha's decision not to participate in the Qatar Grand Prix," MotoGP said in a statement.
"While we recognise the team is subject to a broader corporate policy restricting travel to the Middle East, we do not believe this decision reflects the extensive assurances provided to all championship stakeholders."
Teams are responsible for ensuring their riders attend the Grand Prix. However, it is the governing body of motorcycle racing, FIM, that will decide whether to punish riders who do not show up.
"In addition to the contractual implications of Yamaha's decision for its agreements with MotoGP and IRTA, Yamaha's non-participation also carries sporting implications, with any sporting consequences to be managed by the FIM in accordance with the Championship regulations," MotoGP added.
Aprilia and Ducati, the two leading constructors in the championship this season, had confirmed they would travel to Qatar.
Ducati's championship leader and Malaysian Grand Prix winner Marc Marquez and Aprilia's Jorge Martin are the leading contenders for the title, with the two Spaniards separated by 44 points with three rounds left.
"I go back to Spain and I will arrive in Qatar at the latest time possible, Thursday evening," Marquez said.
Marquez's brother Alex will not travel to Qatar after the Gresini Racing rider opted to undergo shoulder surgery in Madrid and return for the next round in Portugal.
SAFETY 'HIGHEST PRIORITY'
MotoGP said the safety and well-being of everyone in the paddock "remains our highest priority" ahead of the season's final race in Asia before the series returns to Europe for the last two rounds in Portugal and Valencia.
"We will continue to monitor developments closely and remain in regular contact with all relevant authorities and stakeholders," the spokesperson said.
"Decisions of this nature must be based on the most current facts, advice from official sources and informed assessment available at the time they are made. Should that assessment change, we will act accordingly."
Qatar has guaranteed that teams would not be stranded in case of any escalation in the conflict.
Source: Reuters

SINGAPORE – The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) has recalled various chocolate-covered fruit products under the Bomberry brand over concerns
that they may contain metal.
The affected products are Bomberry Natural Blueberries + Belgian Chocolate (150g) in the flavours Dark Chocolate and White & Milk Chocolate, and Bomberry Natural Raspberries + Belgian Chocolate (150g) in the flavours White & Dark Chocolate and White & Milk Chocolate. All four products originate from Australia.
The recall covers products with “best before” dates up to and including Jan 20, 2028.
SFA has directed the importer, Little Farms, to recall the affected products as a precautionary measure, following an earlier recall by Food Standards Australia New Zealand. The recall is ongoing.
Those who have bought the affected products should not consume them, SFA said. Those who have consumed them and have concerns about their health should seek medical advice.
Consumers may contact their point of purchase for inquiries, the agency added.

efet_body:
singapore
SFA recalls various Bomberry fruit snack products over potential presence of metal
The four Bomberry products being recalled over the potential presence of metal.
PHOTO:
Singapore Food Agency
PUBLISHED ON
October 29, 2026
11:47 AM
BY
Sean Ler
The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) is recalling four Bomberry fruit snack products sold here over the potential presence of metal.
In a media release on Thursday (Oct 29), SFA noted that the Food Standards Australia New Zealand has issued a notification on the product recall.
The agency said that it has directed the importer Little Farms to recall the implicated products as a precautionary measure, adding that the recall is ongoing.
According to SFA, the implicated Bomberry products are:
Bomberry natural blueberries + Belgian chocolate (dark chocolate), 150g
Bomberry natural blueberries + Belgian chocolate (white and milk chocolate), 150g
Bomberry natural raspberries + Belgian chocolate (white and dark chocolate), 150g
Bomberry natural raspberries + Belgian chocolate (white and milk chocolate), 150g
All four recalled products originate from Australia and have "best before" dates of up to and including Jan 20, 2028.
Those who have consumed the affected products and have concerns about their health should seek medical attention, while those who have purchased the affected products should not consume them.
They may also approach their point of purchase for enquiries.
Under the Sale of Food Act, foods known to be unsafe for consumption should not be sold.
This is the second case of food product recall in Singapore this week.
On Oct 26, SFA recalled Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding (200g) over the potential presence of glass fragments.

efet_body:
News
Protein pudding sold in S'pore potentially contains glass fragments, SFA issues recall
Crunchy.
Nicolas Wong
October 27, 2026, 02:42 PM
Photo from Singapore Food Authority
The Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding (200g) is being recalled in Singapore.
Singapore Food Agency (SFA) noted in an Oct. 27 press release that the Food Standards Australia New Zealand has issued a recall on the product due to the potential presence of glass fragments.
As a precautionary measure, SFA has therefore
directed its importer (Trade-Pro Food Distribution Pte Ltd) to do the same.
The product originates from Denmark and the batch has a Best Before date of Apr. 28, 2027.
Do not eat it
Under the Sale of Food Act, foods known to be unsafe for consumption should not be sold, SFA said.
It added that consumers who have purchased the affected product should not eat it. They can contact their point of purchase if they have any enquiries.
Those who have consumed the pudding and have concerns about their health should seek medical attention.
Small fragments of glass, if swallowed, usually get coated in bodily fluids and digested food, and are able to pass harmlessly via bowel movements in one to three days.
However, small flecks can also cause superficial scratches to the lining of the throat, esophagus, or stomach, leading to mild sore throat or temporary irritation.

Singapore Food Agency recalled Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding after a possible glass fragment risk was found in the Danish product.
The 200g pudding has a best before date of April 28, 2027, and importer Trade-Pro Food Distribution was told to recall it as a precaution.

AI generated
SINGAPORE –
The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) has recalled a pudding product from a Danish brand, due to the potential presence of glass fragments.
The item is Arla Protein Salted Caramel Flavour Pudding (200g), which originated from Denmark, and
has a “best before” date of April 28, 2027, SFA said in a media statement on Oct 26.
SFA has directed the importer, Trade-Pro Food Distribution, to recall the implicated product as a precautionary measure following an earlier recall by the Food Standards Australia New Zealand.
The recall is ongoing.
The pudding is sold at FairPrice and Cold Storage supermarkets, as well as online marketplaces including GrabMart, Lazada, Redmart, Shopee and FoodPanda.
Those who bought the implicated product should not consume it, SFA said, while those who have consumed it and have concerns about their health should seek medical advice.
Ingesting glass fragments may lead to cuts or tears in the digestive tract. Anyone who experiences chest or abdominal pain, blood in stool, abdominal bloating, or a fever after ingesting the implicated product should seek medical attention.
Consumers may contact their point of purchase for enquiries, the agency added.
